precepts.text: If thy nearest kin entice thee secretly, saying, Let us go and serve other gods, thou shalt not consent unto him nor hearken unto him.
precepts.point: Joshua and Deuteronomy double it: neither make mention of the name of their gods, nor cause to swear by them, neither serve them, nor bow yourselves unto them; and if thy brother or son or wife entice thee secretly, saying, Let us go and serve other gods, thou shalt not consent. Wherever you are, do not go trying to find out how the nations worship their gods.

note.label: Exodus 23: Righteous Judgment, the Three Feasts, and the Angel of the Covenant

precepts.why:
“If thy brother, the son of thy mother, or thy son, or thy daughter, or the wife of thy bosom, or thy friend, which is as thine own soul, entice thee secretly, saying, Let us go and serve other gods, which thou hast not known, thou, nor thy fathers”, whether their gods be “nigh unto thee, or far off from thee, from the one end of the earth even unto the other end of the earth; Thou shalt not consent unto him, nor hearken unto him; neither shall thine eye pity him, neither shalt thou spare, neither shalt thou conceal him”.

That is what making mention of other gods means: going to serve them. Not even your nearest kin can entice you to it. Wherever you are, from one end of the earth to the other, do not go trying to find out how the nations worship their gods.

precepts.text: Mark them which cause divisions and offences contrary to the doctrine which ye have learned, and avoid them.
precepts.point: Going contrary to the laws of marriage, of the sabbath, of raising children righteously, or of going to thy brother alone when there is an ought between you, and secretly enticing others to follow, is how one turns people away from the Lord; those men and those women have to be put out from among the body.

note.label: Deuteronomy 13: Enticers to Other Gods Put Away

precepts.why:
Under the kingdom, the prophet or dreamer of dreams who spoke to turn Israel away from the Lord was put to death. Today Israel is in the land of its oppressors and cannot exact that judgment, and no kind of violence is advocated. What is done today is this: “Now I beseech you, brethren, mark them which cause divisions and offences contrary to the doctrine which ye have learned; and avoid them.”

The one who speaks “to thrust thee out of the way which the Lord thy God commanded thee to walk in” is marked and avoided. Going contrary to the laws of marriage, of the sabbath, of raising children righteously, or of going to thy brother alone when there is an ought between you, and secretly enticing others to follow, is how one turns people away from the Lord. Those men and those women have to be put out from among the body. That is how “So shalt thou put the evil away from the midst of thee” is kept today.

precepts.text: For I give you good doctrine, forsake ye not my law; the doctrine is the law.
precepts.point: Going contrary to the laws of marriage, of the sabbath, of raising children righteously, or of going to thy brother alone when there is an ought between you, and secretly enticing others to follow, is how one turns people away from the Lord; those men and those women have to be put out from among the body.

note.label: Deuteronomy 13: Enticers to Other Gods Put Away

precepts.why:
“For I give you good doctrine, forsake ye not my law.” The doctrine which ye have learned, the doctrine that divisions and offences are marked against, is the law. Good doctrine and the law are one and the same: forsake ye not my law.

So the one who causes divisions and offences contrary to the doctrine is the one going contrary to the laws: of marriage, of the sabbath, of raising children righteously, of going to thy brother alone when there is an ought between you. To speak to turn people away from the Lord their God is to speak against his law, and it is out of the way of that law that the deceiver thrusts them.

precepts.text: The deceived and the deceiver are his; the judgment is the Most High's, not ours.
precepts.point: Going contrary to the laws of marriage, of the sabbath, of raising children righteously, or of going to thy brother alone when there is an ought between you, and secretly enticing others to follow, is how one turns people away from the Lord; those men and those women have to be put out from among the body.

note.label: Deuteronomy 13: Enticers to Other Gods Put Away

precepts.why:
“With him is strength and wisdom: the deceived and the deceiver are his.” Israel today cannot put the prophet or dreamer of dreams to death; we are in the land of our oppressors, and no kind of violence is advocated. The judgment belongs to the Most High, not to us: both the deceived and the deceiver are his, and he will deal with them.

What is ours is to mark them and avoid them, and to put those men and those women out from among the body. The one who has spoken to turn you away from the Lord your God is left in the hand of the one whose he is, with whom is strength and wisdom.

precepts.text: Thou shalt not follow a multitude to do evil; being enticed to serve other gods is evil, so follow them not.
precepts.point: This is why Leviticus 5:1 is opened at the start of class: if you know of anything, you are supposed to utter it. Many grew up on snitches get stitches, but in repentance we have to understand that concealing sin is part of why Israel is in the condition it is in, and we have to teach righteousness. It is that simple.

note.label: Deuteronomy 13: Enticers to Other Gods Put Away

precepts.why:
“Thou shalt not follow a multitude to do evil; neither shalt thou speak in a cause to decline after many to wrest judgment”. Being enticed to serve other gods is evil, so follow them not. Whether it is a multitude, or the one closest to you, thy brother, thy son, thy daughter, the wife of thy bosom, or thy friend which is as thine own soul, saying “Let us go and serve other gods”, the answer is the same: “Thou shalt not consent unto him, nor hearken unto him”.

Nobody can make you do anything, but they can influence you. Following a multitude into evil or following the people nearest you into evil is still following, and the commandment is not to. Do not give anyone that credit and let them cause you to lose your crown.

precepts.text: However close or trusted the person, accept no person against thy soul; your salvation is at stake.
precepts.point: This is why Leviticus 5:1 is opened at the start of class: if you know of anything, you are supposed to utter it. Many grew up on snitches get stitches, but in repentance we have to understand that concealing sin is part of why Israel is in the condition it is in, and we have to teach righteousness. It is that simple.

note.label: Deuteronomy 13: Enticers to Other Gods Put Away

precepts.why:
“Accept no person against thy soul, and let not the reverence of any man cause thee to fall.” The people named here are the closest to you, the ones that can have influence on you: thy brother, thy son, thy daughter, the wife of thy bosom, the friend which is as thine own soul. However close or trusted the person, accept no person against thy soul; your salvation is at stake.

Trust in a person is no cover for your soul. When someone you love and trust has the devil on them, they will lead you astray. That is why the law says “neither shall thine eye pity him, neither shalt thou spare”: the reverence you have for a man cannot be allowed to cause thee to fall. Nobody can make you do anything, but they can influence you; do not give anyone that credit and let them cause you to lose your crown.

precepts.text: If a soul hear the voice of swearing, and is a witness, and do not utter it, he shall bear his iniquity; utter what you know instead of concealing it.
precepts.point: This is why Leviticus 5:1 is opened at the start of class: if you know of anything, you are supposed to utter it. Many grew up on snitches get stitches, but in repentance we have to understand that concealing sin is part of why Israel is in the condition it is in, and we have to teach righteousness. It is that simple.

note.label: Deuteronomy 13: Enticers to Other Gods Put Away

precepts.why:
“And if a soul sin, and hear the voice of swearing, and is a witness, whether he hath seen or known of it; if he do not utter it, then he shall bear his iniquity.” This is why Leviticus 5:1 is opened at the start of class: if you know of anything, you are supposed to utter it. Of the one who entices to other gods the law says “neither shalt thou conceal him”, meaning hide him; when wickedness is concealed, the whole nation is put in jeopardy. When it is uttered and dealt with, “all Israel shall hear, and fear, and shall do no more any such wickedness as this is among you.”

Many grew up on snitches get stitches. But in repentance we have to understand that concealing sin is part of why Israel is in the condition it is in, and we have to teach righteousness. The witness who does not utter what he knows bears the iniquity himself; utter what you know instead of concealing it. It is that simple.

precepts.text: Achan of the tribe of Judah took of the accursed thing, and the anger of the Lord was kindled against the children of Israel.
precepts.point: All Israel stoned Achan with stones and burned him with fire in the valley of Achor, and the Lord turned from the fierceness of his anger; righteous judgment lifted the wrath and the people were able to move forward.

note.label: Deuteronomy 13: Enticers to Other Gods Put Away

precepts.why:
When a city is withdrawn to serve other gods, the law does not strike at once. First “enquire, and make search, and ask diligently”, and only “if it be truth, and the thing certain” is the city smitten with the edge of the sword and burnt with fire. Achan is the example of this kind of judgment.

“But the children of Israel committed a trespass in the accursed thing: for Achan, the son of Carmi, the son of Zabdi, the son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah, took of the accursed thing: and the anger of the Lord was kindled against the children of Israel.” One man of the tribe of Judah took it, and one man's folly kindled the anger of the Lord against all Israel.

Wars Israel had been winning without losing a man began to be lost, and Joshua had to search and seek out who had committed the crime in Israel. That searching is the enquire, make search, and ask diligently of this law, done before anyone was judged.

precepts.text: Joshua and all Israel brought Achan and all he had to the valley of Achor and stoned them with stones; so the Lord turned from the fierceness of his anger.
precepts.point: All Israel stoned Achan with stones and burned him with fire in the valley of Achor, and the Lord turned from the fierceness of his anger; righteous judgment lifted the wrath and the people were able to move forward.

note.label: Deuteronomy 13: Enticers to Other Gods Put Away

precepts.why:
Once the thing was certain, the judgment fell the way this law lays it out. “And Joshua, and all Israel with him, took Achan the son of Zerah, and the silver, and the garment, and the wedge of gold, and his sons, and his daughters, and his oxen, and his asses, and his sheep, and his tent, and all that he had: and they brought them unto the valley of Achor.” All that he had went with him, as the city was to be destroyed utterly, “and all that is therein, and the cattle thereof”, with all the spoil gathered and burnt.

“And all Israel stoned him with stones, and burned them with fire, after they had stoned them with stones. And they raised over him a great heap of stones unto this day.” Stoned, burned with fire, and left a heap, as the city was to be “an heap for ever”.

“So the Lord turned from the fierceness of his anger.” Righteous judgment lifted the wrath, and the people were able to move forward. That is why the place was called the valley of Achor unto this day.
